lines.text: She deserves the only honest one: I don't know - and isn't it wonderful that something is still unknown. Then give her the job. Make her the class sky-watcher: the drawing gets kept, she watches the field on clear nights, and if the lights come back, she draws them again. You've turned a scary question into a scientist's question. And here's the part for you, teacher: file her words and that drawing's date somewhere safe. Twenty years from now she'll either have forgotten completely - in which case nothing was lost - or she won't have, and she'll be one of the few witnesses on Earth with a record from childhood. Either way, you did right by her.
